key_insight: The paper replaces non-associated Coulomb friction with a GSM-compatible associated model by introducing an internal variable tied to asperity-scale plastic deformation, while preserving Coulomb-like behavior over the relevant pressure range.
engineering_relevance: This gives contact mechanics simulations a thermodynamically consistent friction law that can be implemented in FEM and calibrated to realistic tribology behavior, with improved suitability for variational and incremental solvers.
method: Introduce a new internal state variable representing microscopic real contact evolution of rough surfaces.
Drive its evolution through plastic deformation of asperities to recover Coulomb-like friction under non-decreasing contact pressure.
Provide both penalty and Lagrange multiplier formulations for finite element contact analysis.
evidence_signal: A 2D finite element penalty implementation is reported to match classical Coulomb predictions closely on two benchmark tests.
watch_item: The model adds calibration and implementation complexity, and its response depends on the chosen asperity-scale penetration threshold and pressure-history effects.
paper_title: An associated model of Coulomb friction based on the real area of contact
